5.text: The cover of the inner room is held in position by numerous loops

6.text: which are sewed to it, and are passed over two long horizontal poles. The

7.text: rear pole is fastened to the frame of the outer tent. The front pole is sup-

8.text: ported by two forked stakes of sufficient size. These stakes are called “thumbs”

27.text: of which the cover of the inner room is made varies considerably, according

28.text: to the season. In the cold season, while the family is still moving with the

29.text: herd, it is made of the thickest skins with the hair side in, and must be

30.text: renewed every other year, because each bare spot on the surface of the skins

31.text: interferes with the comfort of the inmates. These inner rooms, covered with

32.text: heavy skins, are in use throughout the fall and spring, and among several

33.text: divisions of the tribe — for instance, the people of the Kolyma tundra —

34.text: throughout the whole winter. They are lighted by a single lamp, but heated

35.text: almost exclusively by the animal heat of the dwellers (Plate XIV). Each room

36.text: is of a size proportionate to the number of inmates, and becomes habitable
